title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook — Guide (2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices: incident lifecycle, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates. It is intended as the canonical playbook for engineers, SREs, and support teams responsible for detecting, responding to, and learning from production incidents.

Goals:
- Detect and mitigate user-impacting issues quickly
- Minimize customer-visible downtime and quality regressions
- Triage and escalate clearly with owned responsibilities
- Capture learnings and prevent recurrence

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment support where Redwood provides operational guarantees.
- Includes both user-visible outages (availability, data loss, severe quality regressions) and major internal incidents that can affect SLAs.

Incident severity definitions:
- P0 (SEV0): Complete service outage or data integrity incident affecting all customers, or a critical security incident. Requires immediate page and executive notification.
- P1 (SEV1): Significant degradation or large customer impact (e.g., >10% of requests failing or major latency regression) that materially impacts many users.
- P2 (SEV2): Partial degradation affecting subset of customers or non-critical backend failures that may impact some features.
- P3 (SEV3): Low-impact issues, minor bugs, or cosmetic problems.

SLOs and detection thresholds (examples):
- API availability: 99.95% monthly. Alert if 5-minute availability drops below 99.0% or sustained 30-minute drop below 99.5%.
- P95 latency (text-generate endpoint): target < 300ms for small prompt profiles. Alert if p95 > 600ms for 15m.
- Error rate: Alert if 5xx rate > 0.5% of requests over 5m or >1% over 1m.
- KV cache hit rate: Alert if hit rate drops >10% from baseline for 10m.

Detection and alerting:
- Primary signals: Prometheus / Grafana alerts, PagerDuty pages, real-user monitoring (Sentry / Datadog RUM), status page inbound reports, customer escalations to support.
- PagerDuty: escalation policies per-service (redwood-api, inference-runtime, control-plane). If no ack in 3 minutes escalate to team lead; after 10 minutes escalate to on-call secondary and SRE manager.
- Slack channels: #oncall for real-time coordination, #status-updates for cross-team, #incident-retros for postmortem discussion.

First responder checklist (immediate actions for any P0/P1):
1) Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty and announce in #oncall with severity, short summary, and incident lead (use /incident start template).
2) Triage: check major dashboards (availability, errors, latency), check recent deploys (CI/CD), and look for correlated alerts across services.
3) If customer-impacting, update status page to "Investigating" (see Status Page templates below) within 15 minutes.
4) If live mitigation is possible (e.g., rollback, scale up, switch routing), perform actions following the relevant runbook steps. Document every action and the reason in the incident log.
5) Notify secondary on-call and product/support if escalation criteria met (e.g., >30min to mitigated).

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step):
1) Detect — triggered by alert, customer report, or automated health check.
2) Triage — determine scope, impact, and severity. Assign incident lead.
3) Mitigate — apply mitigations to stop user impact. Prioritize keeping service up over root-cause fixes.
4) Stabilize — monitor indicators for return to normal; consider temporary fixes.
5) Restore — return to fully functional state (may require rollback or config change).
6) Postmortem — produce postmortem within SLA (see Postmortem requirements).
7) Prevent — implement action items and track to completion.

Escalation matrix (high-level):
- On-call engineer → Service owner (via Slack/PagerDuty) → SRE manager → Head of Engineering → CTO (for Sev0/SEV0 with exec impact).

Runbooks (general template for service-level playbooks):
- Runbook title: one-line description.
- Service name(s): e.g., redwood-api-proxy, inference-runtime, kv-cache.
- PagerDuty escalation policy: <policy-id>.
- Detection signals: list of dashboards/alerts to inspect.
- Initial triage steps (1–5 numbered).
- Mitigation steps (rollback, scale, config toggle) with exact commands.
- Post-incident actions and owner.

Example: inference-runtime high-tail-latency runbook
- Service: inference-runtime (k8s namespace: inference-prod)
- Symptoms: p95 latency > 600ms AND queue depth > 500 for 5m
- Initial triage:
  1. Check Grafana dashboard: inference-runtime/p95-latency, queue depth, GPU utilization.
  2. Check recent deploys: ci-cd/last-6h deploys for inference-runtime.
  3. Check autoscaling events: helm get values inference-autoscaler.
- Mitigation options (ordered):
  A) Increase replicas / scale up GPU nodes
     - kubectl -n inference-prod scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=10
     - or trigger cloud autoscaling policy via infra console
  B) Disable expensive model variants: set feature flag runtime.disable-large-checkpoints=true (via config-service)
  C) Rollback to prior stable image: kubectl -n inference-prod set image deploy/inference-runtime inference-runtime=registry/redwood/inference-runtime:20260210-b123
- If mitigation resolves, continue to Stabilize and observe for 30 minutes before marking resolved.

Safe rollback checklist:
- Confirm last deploy time and commit id.
- Ensure compatibility of previous image with current schema/config.
- Notify dependent teams.
- Execute rollback and verify health endpoints return 200 for 2 consecutive minutes.

Postmortem requirements (for P0/P1 and high-impact P2):
- Timeline: publish a draft within 72 hours; final postmortem published within 14 days.
- Authors: incident lead + service owner.
- Must include: summary, impact (customers, duration, SLO breach), timeline of events with timestamps, root cause analysis (why the mitigations were necessary), contributing factors, action items (owner, due date), and lessons learned.
- Classification: "Corrective" (fixes), "Preventive" (process changes), or "Signal" (monitoring/service).
- Postmortem template (outline in content):
  - Title
  - Severity and impacted services
  - Incident summary (one-paragraph)
  - Customer impact and metrics (requests affected, error rate, affected regions)
  - Timeline (table with timestamp, actor, action, notes)
  - Root cause analysis
  - Action items (owner, priority, due date)
  - Follow-up verification criteria

Postmortem publishing and review:
- Post to Confluence under /oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems with label 'postmortem'.
- Review meeting within 7 days including service owner, SRE, product manager, and a representative from support.
- Track action items in JIRA tagged incident-<id>. Action items must have an owner and due date and be reviewed in the weekly SRE triage meeting.

On-call rotations and coverage:
- Primary on-call: 1-week rotation for platform services; shift runs Monday 00:00 UTC to next Monday 00:00 UTC.
- Secondary on-call: 2-week rotation to provide backup coverage; must be available for escalation within 15 minutes.
- PagerDuty policy: primary → after 3 min escalate to secondary → after 10 min escalate to service lead.
- Handoff checklist (on-call shift swap):
  1. Post in #oncall: "Handoff: <name> -> <name>, current open incidents: <list>".
  2. Review open incidents and ongoing mitigations.
  3. Confirm access (PagerDuty, cloud console, runbook links).

Game days (practice and preparedness):
- Frequency: quarterly for major platform areas (api, runtime, caching).
- Goals: validate runbooks, test escalation timing, exercise cross-team comms, and verify automated playbook actions.
- Game day structure:
  1. Design scenario and goals; assign observers and evaluators.
  2. Run scenario in staging with realistic telemetry and injected faults.
  3. Time-to-detection and mitigation metrics recorded.
  4. Debrief with action items assigned; publish game-day report.

Status page and customer communications templates:
- Status page states: Operational, Degraded Performance, Partial Outage, Major Outage, Maintenance.
- Update cadence: Initial "Investigating" update within 15 minutes of confirmed customer impact; regular updates every 30 minutes until mitigated; final summary when incident closed.

Initial status page template:
- Title: [Investigation] Degraded performance for Text Generation API
- Impact: Customers may see elevated latency and 5xx errors on text-generation endpoints.
- Current status: Engineers are investigating.
- What we are doing: Teams are triaging and implementing mitigation steps.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner.

Customer email template (short) for incidents impacting SLAs:
- Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Incident Affecting Text Generation APIs
- Body: We are currently investigating an issue affecting text generation API latency/errors. Our engineering team is actively working to mitigate. We will provide updates via status.redwood.ai and will follow up with a summary and any customer impact after the incident is resolved.

Internal communication checklist:
- Initial Slack announcement in #oncall within 5 minutes.
- PagerDuty page acknowledgement and incident channel created (#incident-<id>).
- Support and sales notified if customers are directly affected.
- Exec notification for P0 within 30 minutes of incident start.

Operational tooling and playbook links (examples):
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/inference-runtime
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.ai/service/<>
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai
- Incident tracker (JIRA): https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INCIDENT-<id>

Access and permissions when responding:
- Ensure you have: PagerDuty, Slack, cloud console IAM for infra team, kubectl with inference-prod context, and read access to logs (Datadog/CloudWatch).
- Emergency access: SRE manager can grant temporary elevated access via access-request workflow (see /confluence/policies-and-process/change-management).

Maintenance and ownership of this playbook:
- Owner: SRE team (eng-sre). Primary document steward: Ava Martinez.
- Review cadence: every 6 months or after any P0/P1 incident.
- Change process: update doc, add a short changelog entry at top, and notify #oncall and eng-sre reviewers for quick sign-off.

Appendices:
A) Incident timeline table example:
Timestamp | Actor | Action | Notes
2026-02-10T14:03Z | pagerduty | Page triggered for redwood-api (5xx spike) | Alert threshold crossed
2026-02-10T14:05Z | oncall-primary | Posted in #oncall and started incident channel | Assigned incident lead
2026-02-10T14:12Z | oncall-primary | Scaled inference-runtime replicas to 10 | Immediate mitigation; reduced queue

B) Postmortem checklist:
- [ ] Draft published in 72 hours
- [ ] Review scheduled with stakeholders within 7 days
- [ ] Action items tracked and triaged in weekly SRE meeting
- [ ] Verification of fixes published

C) Quick commands reference (replace placeholders):
- kubectl -n inference-prod get pods -l app=inference-runtime -o wide
- kubectl -n inference-prod logs deploy/inference-runtime --since=10m | grep ERROR
- jq to inspect config: curl -s https://config-service/api/flags | jq '.runtime'

If you have suggestions for improvements to this playbook, please open an RFC in the eng-sre team backlog or file a PR against this Confluence page.
